top5.title: Jensen Huang steps down as NVIDIA CEO after 33 years
top5.description: Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO of NVIDIA after 33 years. The proposed succession and its consequences for the company are at the center of questions.
top5.why: Jensen Huang’s departure after 33 years would create major uncertainty for NVIDIA’s strategy, leadership succession and valuation at the center of the AI-chip market.

top5.title: Adobe integrates AI agents into Firefly and Creative Cloud creative workflows
top5.description: Adobe is introducing new ways to direct the Creative Agent in Firefly and Creative Cloud to handle complex creative tasks while retaining control over the direction and outcome. Users will be able to delegate repetitive tasks, set their preferences, adjust the agent’s plan, and choose which AI models are used.
top5.why: Adobe’s integration of AI agents into Firefly and Creative Cloud signals a major shift toward delegated creative workflows and could reshape competition in professional software.

top5.title: LangChain reportedly raises 300 million dollars at a 3 billion dollar valuation
top5.description: LangChain, which helps developers build AI agents, reportedly raised 300 million dollars in a deal valuing the company at 3 billion dollars.
top5.why: LangChain’s reported $300 million financing at a $3 billion valuation highlights strong investor conviction in the infrastructure powering enterprise AI agents.

top5.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents make payments after approval
top5.description: OpenAI is beginning to roll out ChatGPT Wallet. The feature allows an AI agent to pay online securely after the user approves the transaction.
top5.why: ChatGPT Wallet moves AI agents toward making approved purchases, a potentially important development for online commerce, payments and consumer-control regulation.

top5.title: Agility goes public as the first publicly traded humanoid company
top5.description: Agility has gone public on the Nasdaq as the first publicly traded company specializing in humanoid robots, with a pre-money valuation of $2.5 billion. However, it generated just $1.8 million in revenue last year.
top5.why: Agility’s public listing gives investors direct exposure to humanoid robotics while testing whether the sector’s ambitious valuations can be justified by still-minimal revenue.
